Graphical Types for a Fitted Model

Source: R/plot_core.R
plot_type.Rd

plot_type is the abstract S7 class of the objects that select a graph of a StatmodFit(). A graph is drawn by autoplot.StatmodFit() (which returns it) or plot.StatmodFit() (which prints it), and the object passed as plot_type decides which graph is drawn and with which options. Three abstract subclasses divide the types by what they read:

  • term_plot: one term of one equation, named by the argument term (plot_effect(), plot_derivative(), plot_shrinkage() and others);

  • model_plot: the fitted distribution as a function of the covariates, without a term (plot_param(), plot_quantiles(), plot_density(), plot_moments());

  • diagnostic_plot: the fit against the data, through the quantile residuals (plot_qq(), plot_worm(), plot_calibration() and others).

Usage

plot_type(label = character(0), legend = TRUE)

term_plot(label = character(0), legend = TRUE)

model_plot(label = character(0), legend = TRUE)

diagnostic_plot(label = character(0), legend = TRUE)

Arguments

label

A single string, the name of the graph.

legend

Whether the graph draws the legend that names its elements. NULL, which a subclass gets when its constructor builds the object from S7::S7_object() without naming legend, draws it as TRUE does.

Value

Nothing: the classes are abstract and their constructors signal an error. Every object that inherits from plot_type has the properties label and legend.

Details

A graph is produced in two steps, each an S7 generic. plot_data() computes the quantities to draw and returns them as a list of data frames; it dispatches on the type and on a second object, the term for a term_plot and the family for the other two. plot_layers() turns that list into ggplot2 layers and dispatches on the type alone. A new type is a subclass of one of the three classes, with a method for each generic.

See also

autoplot.StatmodFit(), plot_data(), plot_layers(), default_plot()

Examples

S7::S7_inherits(plot_effect(), plot_type)
#> [1] TRUE
S7::S7_inherits(plot_effect(), term_plot)
#> [1] TRUE
try(plot_type(label = "mine"))
#> Error in S7::new_object(S7::S7_object(), label = label, legend = legend) : 
#>   Can't construct an object from abstract class <plot_type>
